UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user profile within the Family Hub application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user profile.

profilePicture.description: URL to the user's profile picture.

startTime.description: The start time of the event.

endTime.description: The end time of the event.

attendeeIds.description: References to UserProfiles attending the event. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N Event)

Task.title: Task
Task.description: Represents a task assigned to a family member.

assigneeId.description: Reference to UserProfile assigned to the task. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Task)

dueDate.description: The due date for the task.

completed.description: Indicates whether the task has been completed.

ShoppingListItem.title: ShoppingListItem
ShoppingListItem.description: Represents an item on the shared shopping list.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shopping list item.

quantity.description: The quantity of the item needed.

addedById.description: Reference to UserProfile who added the item. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ShoppingListItem)

purchased.description: Indicates whether the item has been purchased.

Document.title: Document
Document.description: Represents a family document stored within the application.

fileUrl.description: URL to the stored document file.

uploadedById.description: Reference to UserProfile who uploaded the document. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Document)

uploadDate.description: The date and time when the document was uploaded.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore data structure is designed to support the Family Hub application's features, including event calendars, task management, shopping lists, document storage, and user profiles. It prioritizes authorization independence, clarity, and scalability.  User profiles are stored under `/users/{userId}`. Events, tasks, shopping list items, and documents are stored as subcollections of `/users/{userId}` to establish clear ownership and enable secure data access through path-based rules. This eliminates the need for complex `get()` calls in security rules and supports atomic operations.  Each user's data is isolated, enhancing privacy and security. This structure directly supports the required QAPs. Private data is secured through path-based ownership. The segregation of user data into separate collections simplifies security rules. The membership model is implicitly enforced by the path structure, ensuring that only the owner can access their data.
